$note: One indirection between 'this surface wants a picture' and 'here is the file'.
Consumed by resolveArt() in docs/app.js. A 404 on this file is not an error:
every caller falls through to the behavior it had before this file existed.
SHAPE: groups.<group_id>.<slot_name> = { mode, candidates }.
Slots are scoped by group -- a group that declares nothing (or declares an
empty candidate list) resolves to null, which is what pushes its callers onto
the existing fallback tiers. Empty is the normal state, not a broken one.
MODES:
fixed   always candidates[0].
weekly  candidates[week % candidates.length], where week is standings
meta.as_of_week. week is null before the season's first scored
week -- today, for all three groups, and again every rollover --
and a null/non-integer week resolves to candidates[0], i.e.
identical to fixed. Rotation is an addition to day-one behavior,
never a precondition for it.
random  a uniform pick from candidates, independent of week.
rotate  a uniform pick per page load from a MANIFEST this slot names in
`source` rather than from `candidates`, which stays empty. The
manifest is docs-relative, {group} expands in it, and it is
fetched once at boot by the page that owns the slot -- for
hero_banner that is app.js reading data/<group>/banners.json and
joining its `dir` to each `banners[].file`. Selection itself is
the same uniform pick `random` makes; only where the list comes
from differs. A manifest that is missing, empty, 404s or does not
parse leaves the pool empty, which resolves to null -- exactly
what an empty candidate list does -- so the caller lands on its
next fallback tier and nothing about the page breaks.
TOKENS: {group} always expands; per-subject slots also expand {id}.
Substitution runs AFTER selection so rotation never depends on the subject.
by_id (OPTIONAL, per-subject slots only): { <id>: { mode, candidates } }.
Because selection runs before {id} is substituted, ONE group-level list has
to fit every subject in the group -- so a three-variant list written for the
one manager who has three hands the manager who has one a _03 that is a 404.
A subject listed in by_id uses their own spec instead; anyone absent falls
through to the group's. Rotation still happens within the chosen spec only.
CANDIDATE STRINGS are docs-relative image paths, EXCEPT manager_avatar,
whose candidates are size-suffix BASES -- app.js appends _56.webp / _112.webp
to build the 1x/2x srcset pair, exactly as it did before slots existed.
manager_avatar is still gated by assets/portraits/index.json. This file
chooses WHICH avatar a manager gets, never WHETHER they have one; without
that gate a declared candidate would emit an for every manager and put
the 404s the manifest exists to prevent right back.

$why: The ONLY rotate slot in this file. panel has sixteen published banners
(the four managers drawn as coaches, in eight treatments); the other
three groups have exactly one apiece and stay `fixed` -- a rotate slot
with one candidate is a fixed slot that costs an extra request.
`candidates` is empty and that is correct: a rotate slot's pool comes
from `source`, never from a list here. Leaving the old
assets/banners/{group}.webp in candidates would put a SECOND answer to
'which banner' next to the manifest, and the two would drift the first
time build_banners.py published a different set. The single kickoff
banner is still the fallback -- it is reached through the $banners list
in the portraits manifest, one tier down, which is the same tier it
occupied before rotation existed.

REPOINTED from assets/portraits/{group}/{id}.webp. Three directories,
three consumers, one source image each -- they are NOT interchangeable:
assets/profiles/  full-bleed page hero, long edge 1200 (managers.html)
assets/portraits/ 256px poster + face crop for the lightbox rail
img/avatars/      56/112 square crops for the standings rows
Pointing the hero at the 256px poster would upscale it four times over.
mode is `fixed` because panel has exactly one image per manager today.
The day a manager gets a second, this becomes `random` and lists every
variant -- the slot already supports it, no page change required.
The single-manager page (profile.html) ONLY. It is a DIFFERENT SURFACE
from profile_hero, which feeds the roster cards on managers.html, and
that is the whole reason this is a second slot rather than a by_id
override on the first: an override there would push these cuts onto the
roster cards too.
The difference is the cut, not the subject. <id>-ripped.webp is the
torn-right-edge version -- straight on top, left and bottom so it bleeds
into the panel, ragged only where it breaks into the copy column, and
keyed to real alpha so the tear dissolves into the page ground. That
only works where the art sits on paper with nothing around it, which is
profile.html. On a roster card the art is inside a bordered figure,
where a ragged transparent edge reads as a rendering fault, so that
surface keeps the opaque <id>.webp.
Blaine's cut is HAND-PAINTED (from output/personas/panel/panel_blaine_ripped_01.png
via scripts/build_ripped_hero.py) and lands on the same {id}-ripped name
as the generated ones, so he needs no by_id entry -- but do not let
build_profile_heroes.py --force overwrite it. That script skips him.
Everyone else here is generated by scripts/build_profile_heroes.py.
THE MIRROR OF profile_page_hero, and it exists for one reason: the tear
has to open toward the copy. <id>-ripped.webp is ragged on its RIGHT
edge, which is correct for a portrait-LEFT section and wrong for a
portrait-RIGHT one -- there the ragged edge lands against the page
margin, where nothing meets it, and the clean edge butts into the column
it was supposed to break into.
WHICH SECTIONS ASK FOR IT IS NOT A PROPERTY OF THE MANAGER. managers.js
resolves this slot only for sections the alternation places
portrait-RIGHT -- odd profile_order in groups/<group>/personas.json --
and falls back to the right-edge cut when this one is absent from
assets/profiles/heroes.json. That fallback is the normal state for
anyone who has no left cut: reordering personas.json can move a manager
between the two sides without breaking their portrait, it only costs the
tear its direction until the cut is generated.
The left cut is the right cut MIRRORED -- same seed, same tear, alpha
flipped, photograph untouched. Generated by:
python scripts/build_profile_heroes.py --side left --only <group>/<id>
No by_id here. browns/todd rotates two variants on the slot above and is
portrait-LEFT, so he keeps the right-edge cuts he already has. If a
rotating manager ever lands on the right, both variants need a left cut
and this slot needs the same by_id list.
family_comic_01 -- TWO COMIC PANELS, not one scene, and that is a real
constraint made idiomatic rather than a stylistic whim. Gemini carries 5
character-reference slots and family has EIGHT managers, so a single
all-hands render is impossible without dropping three real people. Two
renders of four, composited with a gutter, is what a comic page IS.
Rendered through the decomposed path (--style-spec comic_ink
--composition row), which is the only reason it is correct about who
these people are: the legacy `comic` style hardcodes 'heavy-set college
football head coaches' and GROUP_LOCK asserts 'every man is large and
heavy-set'. This roster is a grandmother, a boy and six others, and its
art is real family photographs, not the fat-coach treatment. The `row`
composition supplies subject='person' and lock='plain' instead.

panel uses. `zach` is on all four rosters with DIFFERENT art on each --

namespace cannot hold them and whichever group shipped second would

ROTATE, on one banner, and that is the point rather than an oversight.
build_banners.py publishes into docs/assets/banners/<group>/ and writes
docs/data/<group>/banners.json -- that IS the rotate slot's input shape.
The `fixed` tier this replaced named the flat assets/banners/browns.webp,
which a DIFFERENT tool writes (prepare_portraits.publish_banner) and which
carries no metadata at all. focal and face_band exist only in the manifest,
and cap_floor / focal_clears_faces in test_banners.py read them from there,
so a `fixed` browns banner could not have carried a measured crop nor been
covered by the guards. Rotate is not a preference here -- it is what
publishing through the script and being framed by the tests both require.
The consequence worth having: banners two through five are a DATA change.
